sources.title: DGII: Tourist Card and countries requiring a Dominican visa
sources.officialityEvidence: DGII's live government page defines the Tourist Card, identifies a named consular-visa cohort, and expressly states the consequence for nationalities outside that list. It is used for its direct named entries and its expressly stated residual rule only.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Los Turistas de los siguientes países no pueden ingresar a República Dominicana con la Tarjeta de Turista

sources.title: MIREX: visas service and Decree 691-07 exception
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX government service describes the consular tourist-visa route and directly limits Decree 691-07 to travellers holding qualifying US, Schengen/EU, Canadian or UK residence or multiple-entry visa documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Pueden ingresar solo con pasaporte válido y una Tarjeta de Turismo para fines turísticos.

sources.title: Decree No. 690-07: named nationals may visit using a Tourist Card
sources.officialityEvidence: The President's Legal Counsel live decree registry returns Decree 690-07, published in Official Gazette 10450. Its operative article expressly names Rumania and Samoa and authorizes Tourist Card entry.
sources.supportingExcerpt: con el simple uso de la Tarjeta de Turismo.

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Romania
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector result is specifically for an ordinary Romanian passport and tourist travel. It answers no visa and directly attributes the result to Decree 690-07, corroborating the controlling decree rather than overriding another source alone.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Pueden ingresar a territorio dominicano en virtud del Decreto 690-07 de fecha 18 de diciembre de 2007

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Samoa
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector result is specifically for an ordinary Samoan passport and tourist travel. It answers no visa and directly attributes the result to Decree 690-07, corroborating the controlling decree rather than overriding another source alone.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Pueden ingresar a territorio dominicano en virtud del Decreto 690-07 de fecha 18 de diciembre de 2007

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Albania
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector is specifically for an ordinary Albanian passport and tourist travel. Its no-visa response explicitly invokes Decree 691-07, which MIREX's live service defines as a qualifying third-country-document exception.
sources.supportingExcerpt: En virtud del Decreto 691-07 de fecha 18 de diciembre de 2007, para fines turísticos exclusivamente.

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Georgia
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector is specifically for an ordinary Georgian passport and tourist travel and returns no visa, but supplies no legal or factual explanation that can reconcile DGII's named consular-visa rule.

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Papua New Guinea
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector is specifically for an ordinary Papua New Guinean passport and tourist travel and returns no visa, but supplies no legal or factual explanation that can reconcile DGII's named consular-visa rule.

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: South Sudan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX selector is specifically for an ordinary South Sudanese passport and tourist travel and answers visa required. It conflicts with DGII's expressly stated Tourist Card residual rule and has no stated legal basis.

policies.title: Romanian and Samoan ordinary passports: Tourist Card without consular visa
policies.summary: Dominican Republic Decree 690-07 expressly names Romania and Samoa for tourist entry with a Tourist Card. Current MIREX ordinary-passport results independently attribute both no-visa outcomes to that decree.
conditions: Applies to a valid ordinary Romanian or Samoan passport for tourist travel only, under Decree 690-07's named Tourist Card route.

The Tourist Card is a tax/formality, not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival or consular visa. DGII states that it permits a tourist stay of up to 30 days and is normally included in foreign-issued air tickets.

Work, study, residence, business, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, special-document, security-screening and final-admission treatment are outside this short-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Albanian ordinary passports: advance Dominican tourist visa baseline
policies.summary: DGII directly names Albania among tourists who cannot enter with a Tourist Card and must obtain a visa at a Dominican mission. MIREX's contrary result invokes only the qualifying-document Decree 691-07 exception.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Albanian passport holder who does not hold the qualifying third-country residence or multiple-entry visa document specified in Decree 691-07.

DGII requires a tourist from Albania to obtain a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission. MIREX states the consular service response time is 10 to 20 business days, so this is an advance visa rather than electronic or arrival issuance.

Decree 691-07 permits tourist entry with a valid passport and Tourist Card only for a traveller with permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, Schengen/EU area, Canada or the United Kingdom; that conditional exception is not this baseline.
Work, study, residence, business, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, special-document, security-screening and final-admission treatment remain outside this finding.

conflicts.explanation: The controlling Decree 690-07 directly names Samoa for Tourist Card entry, and the live MIREX ordinary-passport result attributes its no-visa result to that decree.
DGII directly assigns Albania to the consular-visa cohort. MIREX's no-visa result invokes the document-conditioned Decree 691-07 exception, not an unconditional passport baseline.

conflicts.explanation: DGII directly names Georgia among tourists needing a mission visa, while the live MIREX selector says no visa without a decree, agreement or condition. The fallback advance-visa label is not safely confirmed.

conflicts.explanation: DGII directly names Papua New Guinea among tourists needing a mission visa, while the live MIREX selector says no visa without a decree, agreement or condition. The snapshot's visa-free label is not safely confirmed.

conflicts.officialStatus: unresolved: DGII's closed Tourist Card residual conflicts with the MIREX ordinary-tourist visa-required result
conflicts.explanation: DGII expressly assigns Tourist Card entry to nationalities outside its named visa list, while the live MIREX selector says South Sudan requires a visa without a stated basis. The fallback advance-visa label is not safely confirmed.

unresolved.reason: DGII directly lists Georgia among tourists who must obtain a Dominican mission visa, while the live ordinary-passport MIREX selector says no visa without naming a decree, agreement, condition or issuance route. The conflict cannot be normalized from the selector alone.

DGII directly lists Papua New Guinea among tourists who must obtain a Dominican mission visa, while the live ordinary-passport MIREX selector says no visa without naming a decree, agreement, condition or issuance route. The conflict cannot be normalized from the selector alone.

DGII's expressly stated residual rule assigns a Tourist Card to countries outside its named visa list, which includes South Sudan only by that closed residual. The live ordinary-passport MIREX selector instead says visa required without an explanation, so no route is selected.
